title: Stability Scout: Checklist and Shadow Rollout Log (2026-08) - draft
content:
OVERVIEW:

This is a working draft for the Stability Scout run: a small, controlled 'shadow' rollout that mirrors production traffic into a sandbox path (no user-visible responses) to validate performance, KV cache behaviour, and operational signals before a full canary window. Purpose is to catch regressions in latency P95/P99, memory KV amplification, and tail error modes caused by subtle model/kernel swaps.

GOAL:
- Exercise the exact request shapes we expect in next-week release for 48 hours (span of business-critical peak cycles).
- Validate autoscaling and routing rules for Dedicated pools when model variants are served.
- Surface silent failures (time drift, token corruption, latent rate-limiting) without exposing customers.

SHADOW ROLLOUT DEFINITION (how we run it):
- Mirror: duplicate a % of incoming requests at the LB layer (mirror-tagged) and send to shadow cluster. Shadow returns are dropped; only telemetry captured.
- Traffic shape: 0.5% global mirrored for first 12h, step to 2% for next 12h, then 5% for final 24h if stable.
- Model mapping: shadow serves model-v2 (new quantization/kernels); production continues on model-v1.
- Isolation: shadow cluster uses a Dedicated pool with identical configuration except hardware microcode pinned to candidate version.

PRE-ROLLOUT CHECKLIST (must be green before flip):
- [ ] Release branch merged and infra PR review complete (PR link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Shadow cluster created and annotated in infra inventory (region, pool id).
- [ ] KMS keys accessible to shadow control plane; secrets rotated and verified.
- [ ] Observability: shadow metrics namespace created, dashboards cloned, and alert rules duplicated with -shadow suffix.
- [ ] Synthetic harness loaded with replay dataset (see /test/replays/stability-scout/).
- [ ] KV prefix caching configured to handle repeated replay keys; cache TTL set to 2h for test.
- [ ] Rollback playbook drafted, shared with on-call rotation; escalation tree confirmed.
- [ ] Canary config prepared for automatic fallback to model-v1 on specific thresholds below.

KEY SIGNALS AND GATES (automated and manual):
Automated gates (trigger immediate roll-back of shadow routing):
- p95 latency increase > 30% vs baseline for 10m window (shadow vs baseline-prod).
- Error rate (5xx or model timeouts) > 0.5% absolute for 5m and trending upward.
- Memory footprint per process > +200MB above baseline for 3 consecutive samplings.

Manual gates (requires on-call signoff):
- Any sign of missing or corrupted token sequences in outputs (detected by token-sanity ETL).
- Replica thrashing/oscillation on autoscaler even if latency nominal.

ESCALATION CONTACTS (phone / pager / slack):
- Primary eng oncall (runtime): Marcus Li - pager: pager:marcus - Slack: @marcusl
- Secondary infra: Lina Torres - Slack: @linatorres
- Product owner: Aisha Patel - Slack: @aisha.p

SHADOW RUN CALENDAR (proposed 48h window):
Day 0 - Prep (08:00 - 18:00):
- 08:00: infra spin-up and health-checks (infra@channel).
- 10:00: start synthetic replay at 10% of target shape; validate telemetry pipeline.
- 14:00: full instrumentation smoke (log forwarder, traces, KV sampling).
- 16:00: readiness review, sign-off to start mirrored traffic.

Day 1 - Early mirror (00:00 - 12:00):
- 00:15: mirror 0.5% traffic. Monitor 00:30, 02:00, 06:00 checkpoints.
- 12:00: evaluate metrics and decide step to 2%.

Day 1 - Step-up (12:00 - 24:00):
- 12:00: step to 2%. Longer observation including peak region windows (APAC evening).
- 18:00: quick retro, check autoscaler logs and KV hit ratios.

Day 2 - Final ramp (00:00 - 24:00):
- 00:00: if stable, step to 5% for broader coverage.
- 12:00: run targeted stress tests on burst scenarios (simulate long context tokens).
- 18:00: final assessment. If green, draft release notes and prepare canary schedule.

SMOKE TESTS (short scripts and queries):
- Sanity request: curl -X POST https://shadow-gateway.redwood.internal/generate -H 'X-Shadow: true' -d '{"prompt":"<smoke> short ping"}' 
- KV test: run replay harness with repeat keys and assert hit ratio > 70% after warm-up. (script: ./scripts/kv-warmup.sh --replay=1000)
- Trace sample: ensure traces for shadow requests contain "shadow-cluster-id" tag and span of inference kernel selection.

OBSERVABILITY CHECKS (dashboard queries to snapshot):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (model-inference.*.latency) compare prod vs shadow in same window.
- Token throughput per GPU (tokens/s) and scheduling queue depth.
- KV cache miss ratio by prefix (kv.cache.miss_ratio{prefix=stability-scout}).
- Model divergence sampler: store side-by-side logits hashes for 200 sampled requests to detect silent drift.

ROLLBACK TRIGGERS & STEPS (quick path):
1) Automated gate fired -> infra system sets mirror percentage to 0 and alerts on-call.
2) On-call validates telemetry and escalates if needed.
3) If failure is persistent, tear down shadow cluster; file follow-up ticket and tag release-blocker.

POST-RUN DELIVERABLES (within 48h of end):
- Draft release notes (first pass) included below.
- Incident notes if any gate tripped; add RCA owner.
- Performance deltas table + suggested tuning (batch sizes, kernel fallback).
- Decision: proceed to canary window (Y/N) and proposed canary % and duration.

DRAFT RELEASE NOTES (working copy - do not publish until canary green):
Title: Inference runtime: model-v2 rollout (quantized kernels)
Summary: Candidate release updates kernel selection for Llama-3-variant to new AVX512 kernels and updates quantization profile to Q4-KM. Expected impact: 10-15% token cost reduction, similar or improved P95 tail latency.
Changes:
- Compiler: updated kernel selector that prefers fused-attention for seq<=1024.
- Runtime: improved KV caching prefix eviction to reduce repeated decoding.
- Ops: new observability labels and shadow rollout capability.
Known issues:
- Under some long-context replays, p99 may increase by ~50-70ms (investigating).
- Tokenization edgecases for emoji sequences may regress; mitigation path prepared (token-normalizer toggle).

ACTION ITEMS (owners):
- Marcus: validate and push autoscaler threshold tweak if sustained queue depth observed.
- Lina: confirm log retention for shadow namespace and export of sample traces to S3.
- Aisha: finalize release notes and coordinate canary window with support.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we capture full model outputs for 1 in 10k requests for deep-dive? privacy implications? (need legal ok).
- Is 5% mirror still representative for region-specific peak behaviour? Consider region-targeted ramps.
- Follow-up: run a 7-day extended shadow in staging with traffic shaping to emulate weekend peaks.

Quick links: infra PR, synthesis harness, dash snapshots attached in linked_artifacts.

END OF DRAFT.

Notes: this doc is intentionally lightweight; keep it as the canonical run log for the shadow window. Use this to seed the canary playbook if the run is clean.
